caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.176 of 1995.
lawyer:
BK Das, Advocate, Supreme Court, instructed by Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record —For the Petitioner. 
Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record, Supreme Court — For the Respondents.
parties:
Ajit Kumar Deb ----- Defendant No.4-Petitioner
Vs.
Jyotshna Bikash Dikshit and others ----- Plaintiff-Respondents
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman J: Defendant No. 4—Petitioner calls in question the judgment and order dated 30 November, 1994 passed by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 148 of 1985 (Chittagong), re-numbered as Civil Revision No.1884 of 1991 (Dhaka) discharging the Rule and upholding the judgment and decree passed in Other Appeal No. 2 of 1985 on 26-8-1985 by the Subordinate Judge, First Commercial Court, Chittagong, allowing the appeal upon modifying the judgment and decree passed by the Assistant Judge, First Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 331 of 1979 decreeing the suit in part. 

 2. Plaintiff-respondent No.1 filed the said suit against the petitioner's deceased father Kunja Mohan Deb and others for declaring the deed dated 21-9-76, Exhibit 4 (A), executed by the said Kunja Mohan Deb in favour of his sons appointing them as Shebayets and also for declaring deed of gift Ext. 5 executed by the said Kunja Mohan Deb in favour of his wife, Kamala Bala on 9-10-79 as void, illegal and not binding and also for a further declaration that the said Kunja Mohan Deb is no longer entitled to hold the office of Shebayet of Sree Ragunath Swami family deity and/or his removal and for appointing the plaintiff in his place as Shebayet. The plaint case is that one Kamal Das Mohanta established his family deity Sree Sree Ragunath Jew in a pucca temple in the suit property and the deity was used to be maintained out of income of its properties and the surplus thereof was used to be enjoyed by the members of the family of said Kamal Das Mohanta who was Shebayet and after his death his son Haridas became the Shebayet who died leaving 2 daughters named as Sabitri and Sumitra who became joint shebayets on the basis of compromise decree passed in Other Suit No. 10 of 1952. After the death of Sumitra, Sabitri became the sole Shebayet and she subsequently died leaving son Binode Lal and daughter named Jashoda. The said Binode Lal died leaving no heirs and Jashoda died leaving one daughter Usha, who was married to Monoranjan who resided in that house as ghar jamai. Subsequently Usha died leaving plaintiff Jyotshna Bikash Dikshit and two daughters Badal and Bijoli. Plaintiffs father Monoranjan being insane his maternal grand-mother Sabitri by a deed of gift dated 27-10-1943 Ext. 4 appointed defendant No.1 Kunja Mohan as Shebayet of the said deity and provided for giving maintenance to the minor children of Usha from the surplus income of the said debuttar property. Further case of the plaintiff is that, defendant No. 1 violating the terms of the said deed of gift Ext. 4 did not arrange the Shebapuja of the deity and also did not pay maintenance to the plaintiff and his minor sisters from the income of the debuttar property and misappropriated the entire income. So the plaintiff through his guardian father filed Other Suit No. 10 of 1952 against the defendant No. 1 for his removal from the office of Shebayet and the said suit was decreed on compromise maintaining defendant No. 1 as Shebayet on condition that he would pay monthly allowance of Taka 30.00 to the plaintiff. Defendant No. 1 having not paid the said amount plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 9 of 1958 against defendant No. 1 and the said suit was decreed against him and the decree was upheld upto the appellate Court. Defendant No. 1 removed the plaintiff and his sisters from their residence and their father's shop in the debuttar property treating the same as his own. Defendant No. 1 is unable to work as Shebayet of the deity and failed to manage the debuttar property in terms of the said deed of gift. Defendant No. 1 with the intention of misappropriating the debuttar property gifted properties of schedule 5 to his wife on 9-10-79 by a registered deed Ext. 5 and his wife defendant No. 2 has been trying to transfer the said property to defendant No. 6. Further case of the plaintiff is that, defendant No. 1 illegally appointed his sons defendant Nos. 3-5 as Shebayets after his death by a deed dated 21-9-76 Ext.4(A) though he had no authority to appoint any Shebayet. Plaintiff as heir of Sabitri is entitled to be appointed Shebayet. 

 4. The trial Court decreed the suit in part allowing the plaintiff's prayer in respect of deed of gift Ext. 5 only. On appeal the court of appeal below allowed the appeal and decreed the suit in full declaring the deed of shebayetnama Ext. 4(a) dated 21-9-76 executed by defendant No. 1 in favour of his sons defendant Nos. 3-5 as illegal and void and also appointed plaintiff as Shebayet of the deity removing defendant Nos. 3-5 from the office of Shebayet.
